title: Market Entry Pack & Terms — Quick Slate (WIP)
content:
Purpose: quick, product-facing pack to accelerate partner marketplace submissions (AWS/Azure/GCP) + initial terms/entitlements template. This is intentionally lightweight — not the final legal doc — meant for engineering, product, and partner managers to get a listing live while we finalize contract language.

Status: WIP. Focus for next two sprints: SKU naming alignment, pricing unit normalization, and gating checklist for compliance and telemetry.

Audience: partner manager, solution engineer, listing copy owner, billing engineer, enterprise legal (FYI).

Goals:
- Produce a single package (tile copy + assets + SKU map + entitlement rules) deployable to cloud marketplace vendor consoles with minimal back-and-forth.
- Provide a small, auditable checklist for security/compliance gating (KMS / data residency / SOC/ISO flags).
- Ship a default pricing/usage mapping that engineering can implement as billing events.

High-level constraints / assumptions:
- This is for Hosted API product first (no Dedicated/Private SKUs in initial launch).
- Billing model: usage-based (token units) with optional committed monthly reserved capacity SKU (beta).
- Each cloud marketplace requires 1) tile + short desc + long desc, 2) at least one SKU for billing, 3) technical listing metadata (region availability, SLA tier).

Tile and copy snippets (first pass)
- Tile headline (12–20 chars): "Redwood Inference API"
- One-line elevator (40–140 chars): "High-throughput LLM inference: predictable latency, cost controls, and secure deployments."
- Short description (60–220 chars): "Run text generation, chat, and embeddings with a production-grade inference API — streaming responses, intelligent batching, and transparent performance analytics."
- Long description (350–800 chars): "Redwood Inference delivers a unified inference platform for teams building LLM features. Choose hosted, reserved, or private deployment modes. Benefit from kernel-optimized runtime, auto-batching, prefix caching, and integrated observability that ties latency, cost, and quality back to routes and prompts. Ideal for product teams requiring predictable performance and enterprise controls (SLA, VPC, KMS). See docs and quickstart for SDKs and sample apps."
- Bullet highlights (to insert into marketplace features list):
  - Production-first serving runtime with predictable latency
  - Model catalog and version pinning
  - Streaming and function-calling support
  - Token-level cost visibility and per-route analytics
  - Enterprise controls: VPC, KMS, audit logs

SKU & pricing draft (naming conventions)
- SKU pattern: RW-<CLOUD>-<OFFER>-<UNIT>-<TIER>
  - Example: RW-AWS-HOSTED-TOKENS-PAYG
  - Reserved example: RW-GCP-DEDICATED-GPU-MONTHLY-8X
- Units: TOKENS (1000-token increments), EMBEDS (per-embedding), RESERVED-HOURS (for Dedicated pools)
- Pricing guidance (placeholder):
  - PAYG tokens: $0.00045 per token unit (1 token unit = 1k tokens)
  - Embeddings: $0.0008 per embedding
  - Reserved capacity: fixed monthly price depending on instance size (engineering to supply mapping)
- Billing events required: request_id, model_id, tokens_consumed, route_id, org_id, offer_sku

Entitlement & feature flags mapping
- Default entitlements for marketplace customers: Hosted API access, standard telemetry (30d retention), basic support (email).
- Optional add-ons (separate SKUs):
  - Audit-logs retention +90d (compliance add-on)
  - Private deployment / VPC (entitlement requires legal + provisioning SLA)
  - Dedicated reserved units (commit contract + provisioning lead time)

Compliance and gating checklist (pre-submit)
- Legal: standard T&Cs + marketplace-specific contract layer (legal to confirm) — JIRA-PRJ-4821
- Security: confirm encryption at rest (KMS) and in transit; list supported KMS providers per cloud
- Data residency: declare regions where hosted product will accept customer data (EU, US, APAC)
- Logging: confirm telemetry does not expose PII; outline retention and redaction policy
- Certifications: indicate SOC2 status and ISO if available; include cert URLs in listing

Technical QA matrix (minimum tests before publish)
- Tile loads and assets render on vendor console (pass/fail)
- Acceptance test: basic generate API call from marketplace-linked account using test key
- Billing test: simulated token usage triggers billing webhook with correct SKU mapping
- Entitlement test: ensure marketplace-created account receives the correct role/limits
- Integration test: SDK quickstart against marketplace provisioned tenant

Upload assets (required)
- 1024x1024 logo (square, PNG) — filename: rw-logo-1024.png
- 1200x628 hero banner (JPEG) — filename: rw-hero-1200x628.jpg
- 30s demo video link + transcript (hosted S3)
- Short PDF one-pager (product + pricing)

Sample acceptance email to partner (template)
- Subject: "Redwood listing live — quick steps to onboard"
- Body: brief: listing published, steps to claim account, contact for support, pointer to integration guide + billing test instructions

Rollout plan (phases)
- Phase A (internal beta): limited partners, manual provisioning, collect telemetry on latency/cost and docs clarity (2 weeks)
- Phase B (public listing soft launch): enable PAYG SKUs, enable billing automation, monitor for chargeback issues (4 weeks)
- Phase C (GA): add reserved capacity SKUs, entitlement automation, surface in partner portal (dependent on legal sign-off)

Open questions / decisions needed (owner tags)
- Reserved pricing tiers: need infra input on per-GPU throughput and cost baseline — owner: Noah Becker (eng-infra)
- Marketplace contract addendum template: legal to provide short appendix for marketplace transactions — owner: Priya Rao
- KMS provider mapping per cloud: operations to confirm supported integrations — owner: Liam Chen

Next steps (this week)
- Finalize tile copy and short/long descriptions (owner: Asha) by 2025-03-07
- Create placeholder SKUs in billing repo and stub webhooks for test (owner: Billing eng) — JIRA-PRJ-4825
- Attach assets and demo video link in vendor consoles (owner: GTM ops)
- Schedule legal review meeting to produce marketplace addendum (owner: Priya)

Notes to self:
- Keep copy concise for vendor consoles; add deeper product docs link rather than stuffing features into the long description.
- We should capture which analytics labels will be surfaced back to vendor (e.g., route_id) — useful for cost allocation.

Attachments: see linked_artifacts.

If you make edits, add a one-line change note at top and update last_modified.
